Scent
sĕnt
n. (smell, savour; in Scripture a figure of hidden life, of settled complacency, and of revival)
Old French sentir, to feel or perceive, from Latin sentire. In Job the word is reyach, the same term used of the sweet savour of sacrifice — what rises from a thing and tells you what it is.

Biblical Definition

Job makes the scent of water the emblem of hope in a dead thing: “Yet through the scent of water it will bud, and bring forth boughs like a plant” (Job 14:9) — a felled tree that smells rain and lives. Jeremiah makes it the emblem of a nation that has never been disturbed: Moab “hath settled on his lees, and hath not been emptied from vessel to vessel, neither hath he gone into captivity: therefore his taste remained in him, and his scent is not changed” (Jer 48:11). Hosea makes it the emblem of restoration: “they shall revive as the corn, and grow as the vine: the scent thereof shall be as the wine of Lebanon” (Hos 14:7).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines scent as odor; smell; that substance which, emitted from a body, affects the olfactory organs; and also the power of smelling.

expand to see more

SCENT, n. Odor; smell; that substance which, emitted from any body, affects the olfactory organs of animals.

SCENT, n. The power of smelling; the smell; as a hound of nice scent.

SAVOR, n. Taste or odor; something that perceptibly affects the organs of taste and smell.

Key Scripture

Job 14:9 — "Yet through the scent of water it will bud, and bring forth boughs like a plant."

Jer 48:11 — "Moab hath been at ease from his youth, and he hath settled on his lees, and hath not been emptied from vessel to vessel, neither hath he gone into captivity: therefore his taste remained in him, and his scent is not changed."

Hos 14:7 — "They that dwell under his shadow shall return; they shall revive as the corn, and grow as the vine: the scent thereof shall be as the wine of Lebanon."

Job 9:10 — "Which doeth great things past finding out; yea, and wonders without number."

Modern Corruption

Jeremiah names undisturbed ease as a judgment rather than a blessing, since Moab kept his flavour only because he was never poured out.

expand to see more

Jeremiah 48:11 is a winemaker's sentence turned into a doctrine. Wine left on its lees keeps its old taste and never improves; it must be racked from vessel to vessel to be refined. Moab had never been racked. He had been at ease from his youth, never emptied, never carried away, and the result was not maturity but a nation whose scent was not changed — the same at the end as at the beginning, and about to be broken for it. Ease is treated here as the absence of God's refining, and Scripture is consistent about it: whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and if ye be without chastisement, then are ye bastards and not sons.

The corruption to name is the assumption, widespread and rarely stated, that an untroubled life is evidence of God's favour and a hard one evidence of His displeasure. Psalm 73 works through it honestly — Asaph envied the prosperity of the wicked until he went into the sanctuary and understood their end. Hebrews 12 works through it doctrinally. Jeremiah 48 works through it by taking a nation that had everything the modern definition of blessing requires and calling its condition a judgment. The scent that pleases God is the one that comes off a life He has poured from vessel to vessel.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew reyach (H7381), scent, savour, smell; shemer (H8105), lees or dregs; chayah (H2421), to live, revive.

expand to see more

Hebrew reyach (H7381) — scent, savour; Job 14:9, Jeremiah 48:11, Genesis 8:21.

Hebrew shemer (H8105) — lees, dregs of wine; Jeremiah 48:11, Zephaniah 1:12.

Hebrew chayah (H2421) — to live, revive, quicken; Hosea 14:7, Psalm 119:25.

Hebrew shaanan (H7599) — to be at ease, secure; Jeremiah 48:11, Amos 6:1.

Greek osme (G3744) — odour, savour; 2 Corinthians 2:14, Philippians 4:18.

Usage

"“Through the scent of water it will bud” — the felled tree that smells rain."

"“His scent is not changed” — Moab, never emptied from vessel to vessel."

"“The scent thereof shall be as the wine of Lebanon” — Hosea on revival."
